newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end slightly lower in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end slightly lower in moderate trade.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed softer for the fifth session in a row on Wednesday, although the loss was smaller than in previous sessions with the market buoyed by bargain-hunting, traders said.
The bolsa is expected to open relatively stable with investors keeping a close watch on long-term interest rates, which have risen recently, they said.
The 40-share IPSA index closed down 0.08 percent at 87.95 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.17 percent to 4,868.79 points in turnover of 14.2 billion pesos.

Long-term interest have risen recently as investors bet that the Central Bank will only ease its current credit squeeze in the second quarter of next year, rather than in the first quarter as the market had originally expected, said traders.
Eight year rates closed at 6.23 percent, up from 6.14 percent last week.

Telecoms company CTC rose for the second session in a row on news that a consortium in which it is a partner won an auction for a 35 percent stake in Brazilian telephone company CRT Tuesday, dealers said.
CTC ended up 0.85 percent at 2,370 pesos.
Declining issues included electricity utility Edelnor, which tumbled on the company's poor results, said traders.
The firm reported nine month earnings of 800 million pesos this year against 6.4 billion pesos in the same period 1995.
Edelnor closed off 7.14 percent at 195 pesos.
Other decliners included telecoms company Telex, down 2.11 percent at 930 pesos and forestry firm Masisa which shed 0.59 percent at 169 pesos.
